cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Not Until You Explain
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wait. You said you were at work until six. This taxi receipt says five. Let's get the times straight before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was five when I left. That's my bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then six wasn't leaving work. Was it getting home? One event per time, please. I'll drive you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six was when I reached the hotel. I wasn't ready to tell you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. We're up to the hotel. Put your bag down and tell me why you went there.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 demands chronological precision and A3 corrects the meaning of six rather than merely accusing B. A5 keeps B present by advancing to the disclosed hotel in A's controlled inquiry.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 admits five and invokes the bus. A3 offers a lift while separating departure from arrival; B4 answers that distinction with the hotel, causing A5's next question.

relationship.evidence: B2 needs transport and B4 is reluctant to disclose a destination. A's lift removes a practical pressure without inventing an authority to detain B.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's new destination to deepen the inquiry instead of returning to the already resolved departure time.

specificity.evidence: A1 states both conflicting times and their sources. B4 supplies the hotel as new information; the reader need not invent why B was there to understand the demand.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's one-event-per-time instruction makes A's method audible. A5's thanks and narrowed question are directed at keeping B talking.

coach2.situation: A1 states both conflicting times and their sources. B4 supplies the hotel as new information; the reader need not invent why B was there to understand the demand.
coach2.stated: A1 work-until-six conflicts with a five taxi receipt; B2 admits departure at five; A3 offers a drive; B4 identifies hotel arrival at six.
coach2.inferred: A knows B's earlier account and cares about the omission; no specific romantic or criminal backstory is required.
coach2.missing: The hotel purpose is the information A is seeking, not a premise the reader must supply.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate found; A's bag instruction is an ordinary way to ask the departing person to stay.

reservation: The supervisory professionalism is quieter than occupational expertise, but the chronology corrections give it a real tactic. No inference of actual detention is intended.
provenance: Explicit direct assistant assessment/rereading; not fresh, independent, human, or worker proof.
